contract.title: Project deterministic SVG from presentation authority

intent.trigger: one pinned presentation schema, presentation contract, and SVG projection profile are submitted
intent.need: project the declared visual subject through one generic deterministic SVG interpreter
intent.purpose: produce byte-stable SVG and independently verifiable conformance evidence without renderer discretion

constraints.text: The presentation schema alone defines which presentation declarations are legal.
The presentation contract alone defines sections, text, order, bounds, colors, fonts, icons, omission policy, and rewriting policy.
The projection profile identifies the renderer catalog, theme catalog, primitive catalog, icon catalog, output path, and serialization policy.
The CLI receives one context JSON path and resolves schema.schemaPath, contract.contractPath, projection.profilePath, and projection.outputPath relative to the context file directory.
Every referenced schema, contract, and profile file must exist, parse as JSON, and be consumed; missing or invalid referenced bytes are terminal RED and no default authority is permitted.
Schema, contract, and profile hashes are SHA-256 identities of the exact referenced file bytes, not reconstructed or reserialized JSON.
The parsed presentation contract must validate against the parsed referenced presentation schema before a projection plan is resolved.
The complete resolved projection plan is serialized deterministically to generated/resolved-projection-plan.json and its hash is computed from those exact bytes.
Fallback canvas sizes, fallback operations, fallback artifact identities, hard-coded SVG content, and unconditional PASS observations are forbidden.
The SVG projection kernel contains no infographic-specific branching and makes no visual design decisions.

The primitive catalog is closed to create-svg-root, create-group, create-rectangle, create-line, create-path, create-text, create-tspan, create-icon, apply-transform, apply-style-token, bind-content, clip-region, and serialize-svg.

The initial renderer catalog is closed to split-hero, three-equal-cards, three-equal-columns, split-callout-with-center-divider, three-step-horizontal-journey, capability-equation, horizontal-banner, right-outcome-callout, and single-line-footer.
Every icon resolves from a pinned registry to declared viewBox and path data; external assets and substitutions are forbidden.

SVG serialization uses UTF-8, LF endings, canonical attribute order, projection-sequence element order, fixed numeric precision, no timestamps, no random identifiers, no runtime comments, stable whitespace, and one terminal newline.
Conformance inspection parses emitted SVG bytes and compares observed structure with authority without trusting projector claims.
The acceptance algorithm evaluates ordered checks and returns the first assigned RED code; GREEN is forbidden when any required check fails.
All implementation artifacts project beneath capabilities/project-deterministic-svg-from-presentation-authority using canonical scenario and responsibility folders.

outcome.statement: One admitted presentation authority produces one canonical SVG artifact and one terminal conformance receipt.

observableState.text: The exact submitted presentation contract is validated and consumed.
One complete ordered projection plan resolves every section, bound, binding, token, icon, renderer, and proof requirement.
Repeated projection from identical authority produces byte-identical SVG.
The receipt binds schema, contract, profile, plan, and SVG hashes to the terminal disposition.
Every invalid authority or artifact condition returns its assigned first RED code.

feature.title: Project deterministic SVG from presentation authority

userStory.iWant: a presentation schema, presentation contract, and projection profile to drive one generic SVG projection kernel
userStory.soThat: the declared visual subject is embodied and independently verified without renderer discretion or byte drift

feature.governingObligation: Transform only admitted presentation authority into canonical SVG bytes and a conformance receipt without infographic-specific branching or undeclared visual decisions.

background.text: one immutable presentation schema identifies the admissible presentation language
one immutable presentation contract identifies the exact visual subject
one immutable projection profile identifies rendering and serialization policy
the renderer, theme, primitive, and icon registries are pinned and available

given.text: the pinned schema, contract, profile, and registries are available as exact bytes
one context JSON path identifies all referenced authority files and the SVG output path

when.text: the resolver reads the context, resolves each referenced path relative to it, hashes exact bytes, validates the contract against the schema, and resolves layouts, content bindings, and proof requirements

then.text: one ambiguity-free ordered SVG projection plan is returned
any missing, unknown, inconsistent, or unresolvable declaration is rejected before projection
no fallback canvas, operation, identity, content, or profile is introduced

obligation.statement: Resolve all presentation decisions before SVG element creation.

signal.statement: One complete resolved projection plan is observable.

scenarios.title: Execute the resolved plan without visual discretion

given.text: one validated projection plan contains exact operations, bounds, bindings, tokens, and renderer identities

when.text: the generic projection kernel executes every operation in declared sequence

then.text: each emitted SVG element corresponds to one admitted operation
no artifact-specific branch, external asset, substitution, or inferred design decision is introduced

obligation.statement: Mechanically interpret the resolved plan through bounded generic primitives and renderers.

signal.statement: The complete admitted SVG element tree is observable.

given.text: one complete in-memory SVG tree contains only admitted elements and attributes

when.text: the canonical serializer orders and encodes the tree under the pinned policy

then.text: identical authority produces byte-identical UTF-8 SVG with LF endings and one terminal newline
timestamps, random identifiers, runtime comments, and unstable whitespace are absent

obligation.statement: Emit canonical SVG bytes whose identity depends only on admitted authority.

signal.statement: Exact canonical SVG bytes and their hash are observable.

given.text: the exact emitted SVG bytes and admitted presentation authority are available

when.text: the inspector parses the SVG and evaluates identities, order, bounds, text, tokens, icons, overflow, and undeclared elements

then.text: one ordered observation exists for every proof requirement
observed SVG state is compared with authority without trusting projector claims

obligation.statement: Observe generated SVG structure and presentation semantics independently of projection execution.

signal.statement: Complete ordered proof observations are observable.

given.text: all ordered proof observations and exact input, plan, and SVG hashes are available

when.text: the evaluator applies the fail-closed acceptance algorithm

then.text: INFOGRAPHIC_CONFORMS is issued only when every required check passes
the first failed check returns its assigned terminal RED code and no GREEN receipt

obligation.statement: Bind exact authority and artifact identities to one exhaustive terminal disposition.

signal.statement: One terminal receipt binding all required hashes and findings is observable.

implementationBoundary.text: Projection is performed by the generic deterministic capability projector directly from this schema-valid contract; no conveyor stage, runtime, adapter, model, or feature-specific projector participates.
Every materialized path, artifact role, scenario binding, entrypoint, dependency permission, projection form, source token, and expected byte hash is declared in this contract.
The projected capability may import Node.js runtime modules declared by dependency policy and relative files declared inside its own capability root, but no file outside that root.

implementationExitConditions.text: Projection into an empty root produces exactly the declared artifact set and every artifact matches its declared SHA-256 identity.
A copy containing only the projected capability folder executes its declared verification entrypoint successfully.
Unknown contract properties, undeclared artifacts, path escapes, unbound scenario bodies, forbidden imports, and byte drift are rejected fail-closed.
